title: Working Capital
author: oA7a2DXCeN3DLamvj
chapter_outcomes: Explain why businesses need finance, including start-up capital, expansion and working capital, and distinguish between short-term and long-term finance needs.

Explain internal and external sources of finance with examples, distinguish between short-term and long-term finance, evaluate alternative sources of capital, analyse factors influencing financial choice, and recommend and justify appropriate sources of finance in given circumstances.
Explain the importance of cash to a business, construct, amend and interpret simple cash-flow forecasts and their importance, and evaluate methods of overcoming short-term cash-flow problems.
Explain the concept and importance of working capital to a business.
Explain what profit is, how it is generated, why it is important to private sector businesses, and distinguish between profit and cash.
Explain the main features of an income statement (e.g. revenue, cost of sale, profits) and use profit information from simple income statements to support business decision-making.
Explain the main elements of a statement of financial position, including classifications of assets and liabilities using examples.
Interpret a simple statement of financial position and make deductions from it, e.g. how a business is financing its activities and what assets it owns, sale of inventories to raise finance.
Explain the concept and importance of profitability to a business.
Explain the concept and importance of liquidity to a business.

Interpret financial performance by calculating and analysing profitability and liquidity ratios, including gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio and acid test ratio.
Explain why accounts and ratio analysis are used, identify the needs of different users of accounts, and analyse how this information supports business decision-making.
